- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- If model shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising prices) with negative sentiment, cap forecast rise at 1–2% above recent high to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.20) and model is flat or slightly falling, model underestimates mean reversion; adjust downward by 2–5% to align with recent mean.
- If true outcome shows sharp drop after model spike, apply lag correction: reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3–5 days post-spike.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in cycle; apply 1–3% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive -0.15+), model tends to overreact; apply 5–10% downward adjustment to forecast peak.
